questions.q: What do the four letters of SPIN stand for?
a: Situation, problem, implication, need-payoff
Story, pitch, interest, negotiation
Situation, product, incentive, network
Service, price, innovation, need
questions.why: Lesson 1 lays out the four kinds of questions that make up the SPIN method.

questions.q: What is the purpose of implication questions?
a: To help the client see how serious their problem is
To gather basic facts about their current setup
To find out what they intend to do about the problem
To compare your price with your competitors’ prices
questions.why: Lesson 1 says implication questions reveal the consequences of a problem the client has been treating as minor.

questions.q: How does the summary define a feature?
a: A bare fact about the product that does little to sell it
A promise about what the product will do for the buyer
A need the customer already knows they have
A discount offered to close the deal
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls features mere facts, like RAM or screen size, which most buyers barely understand.

questions.q: What makes a benefit different from an advantage?
a: It matches the product’s ability to a specific need the client has
It lists more technical specifications than an advantage
It is only used when closing the sale
It focuses on the company rather than the customer
questions.why: Lesson 2 says benefits connect what the product does with what matters to that particular client.

questions.q: How does the summary recommend learning the SPIN technique?
a: Practice one stage at a time and accept a lot of mistakes
Master all four stages in a single intensive session
Study the theory until you can recite it perfectly
Try it first on your most important clients
questions.why: Lesson 3 advises one step at a time, quantity of attempts over polish, and practice on smaller clients first.
